body: Adult social care services in England are regulated and inspected by
explanation: CQC asks whether services are safe, effective, caring, responsive and well-led.

subject: CWR
body: The Care Act 2014 puts a duty on local authorities to promote people's
explanation: Wellbeing covers dignity, control, relationships, safety and more.

subject: CWR
body: The Mental Capacity Act 2005 says a person must be assumed to have capacity
options: unless it is established that they lack it
explanation: This is the first of its five principles.

subject: CWR
body: Under the Mental Capacity Act, making an unwise decision
options: does not on its own mean a person lacks capacity
must be reported to the police
explanation: People have the right to make choices others disagree with.

subject: CWR
body: If a person lacks capacity, any decision made for them must be in their
options: best interests and the least restrictive option
explanation: Involve the person as much as possible.

subject: CWR
body: The duty of candour means providers must
options: be open and honest with people when things go wrong
only tell the CQC about errors
explanation: This includes giving an apology and explanation.

subject: CWR
body: Which of these is one of the six principles of adult safeguarding?
explanation: The others are prevention, proportionality, protection, partnership and accountability.

subject: CWR
body: Taking money from a person's purse without permission is
explanation: Report concerns through your safeguarding procedure.

subject: CWR
body: Repeatedly failing to give a person the care they need, such as food or medication, is
explanation: Neglect can be deliberate or through poor practice.

subject: CWR
body: Poor practice that is built into how a whole care service runs is called
explanation: Examples are rigid routines and lack of choice.

subject: CWR
body: If someone tells you they are being abused, you should
options: promise to keep it a secret
listen, reassure them and explain you must share the information
explanation: Report it promptly following your safeguarding procedure.

subject: CWR
body: Whistleblowing means
options: using a whistle in an emergency
reporting wrongdoing at work that is in the public interest
explanation: Whistleblowers are protected by law.

subject: CWR
body: Active listening includes
options: planning your reply while they speak
giving full attention and checking you have understood
explanation: Use open body language and summarise back.

subject: CWR
body: When supporting someone with hearing loss, you should
options: face them, speak clearly and reduce background noise
explanation: Check hearing aids are working.

subject: CWR
body: An open question is one that
options: invites a fuller answer, such as 'How are you feeling today?'
can only be answered yes or no
explanation: Closed questions are useful for quick facts.

subject: CWR
body: Person-centred care means
options: care that suits the staff rota
care planned around the person's needs, wishes and preferences
explanation: The person should be involved in decisions.

subject: CWR
body: Respecting dignity during personal care includes
options: closing doors and curtains and keeping the person covered
leaving the door open to save time
explanation: Ask for consent before you start.

subject: CWR
body: Before providing care or support, you should
options: tell them what will happen next week
explanation: Consent can be given verbally, in writing or by gestures.

subject: CWR
body: The single most effective way to prevent the spread of infection is
explanation: Wash or use alcohol rub before and after contact.

subject: CWR
body: When taking off PPE, gloves are usually removed
explanation: Follow your local procedure and wash your hands after removing PPE.

subject: CWR
body: Alcohol hand rub does not work well against
explanation: Use soap and water in these cases.

subject: CWR
body: Used sharps such as needles must be
options: put straight into a sharps bin without re-sheathing
put in a general waste bag
left on a tray for later
explanation: Never fill a sharps bin past the fill line.

subject: CWR
body: If a person's mobility has changed and you're unsure about a transfer, you should
options: stop and ask for the moving and handling plan to be reviewed
explanation: Only use equipment you are trained to use.

subject: CWR
body: Before using a hoist, you should check
options: nothing if it was used yesterday
the sling size and condition and the hoist's service date
explanation: Follow the person's care plan.

subject: CWR
body: Signs of dehydration include
options: dark urine, confusion and a dry mouth
explanation: Offer drinks regularly and record intake if required.

subject: CWR
body: Pressure ulcers are most likely to develop
options: on the palms of the hands
over bony areas such as heels, hips and the base of the spine
explanation: Regular repositioning and skin checks help prevent them.

subject: CWR
body: A sudden change in a person's confusion could be a sign of
options: infection, such as a urinary tract infection
explanation: Report changes promptly.

subject: CWR
body: The FAST test for stroke stands for Face, Arms, Speech and
explanation: Act quickly; every minute counts.

subject: CWR
body: Care workers should only give medication if they
options: are trained, assessed as competent and follow the care plan
are asked by the person's relative
explanation: Record every administration on the MAR chart.

subject: CWR
body: If a person refuses their medication, you should
options: respect the refusal, record it and report it
explanation: Covert medication needs a formal assessment and plan.

subject: CWR
body: Care records should be
explanation: Records may be used as legal evidence.

subject: CWR
body: Information about the people you support should be shared
options: on social media if names are hidden
with your friends if it's interesting
only on a need-to-know basis following policy
explanation: Data protection law applies.

subject: CWR
body: Treating someone less favourably because of their religion is
explanation: This is unlawful under the Equality Act 2010.

subject: CWR
body: A reasonable adjustment is
options: a change made so a disabled person isn't disadvantaged
explanation: Examples include easy-read information or ramps.

subject: CWR
body: When supporting a person with dementia who is distressed, you should
options: stay calm, reassure them and try to understand what they need
talk about them to others in front of them
leave them alone for the shift
explanation: Distress is often a way of communicating a need.

subject: CWR
body: A duty of care means
options: acting in the best interests of the people you support and keeping them safe
doing whatever the person asks, even if unsafe
avoiding all risks for the person
explanation: Balance rights and risks; seek advice when unsure.

subject: CWR
body: If you are asked to do a task you haven't been trained for, you should
options: search for a video and then do it
explain this to your manager and ask for training
ask a person you support to show you
explanation: Work within your competence.

subject: CWR
body: For an adult who is not breathing normally, you should give
explanation: Call 999 and get an AED.

subject: CWR
body: A person's dietary needs and preferences should be
options: recorded in their care plan and respected
explanation: Consider allergies, culture, religion and swallowing needs.

subject: CWR
body: Someone with swallowing difficulties (dysphagia) may need
options: food and drinks of a modified texture as advised by a speech and language therapist
explanation: Follow the IDDSI level in their care plan.
